items.h: Jahan Dotson a Touchdown-Dependent Flex Play in Week 8
items.s: Atlanta Falcons wide receiver Jahan Dotson disappointed in Week 7, notching just one catch (three targets) for six yards after a solid three-game stretch that saw him average over two catches and 65 yards per game while recording a pair of touchdown catches over that span. Quarterback Michael Penix Jr. targeted 10 different receivers in last week's contest, so there were likely going to be some underwhelming performances from players not named Drake London, Kyle Pitts Sr, and Bijan Robinson. Still, the Penn State product had the highest average depth of target on the team (19 yards), which has been the case all season (16.9 yards), so he's always a home run threat. Week 8 brings a touch…

items.h: Only one catch in Week 7 victory
items.s: Dotson caught one pass on three targets for six yards during Sundays' 29-20 win over San Francisco. Dotson's lone catch came late in the second quarter as part of a 14-play, 56-yard drive that ended with a 33-yard field goal by Nick Folk as time expired. Dotson also drew a defensive pass interference penalty late in the third quarter, but it was an otherwise quiet night for the fifth-year pro, whose 38 offensive snaps were second-most among Falcons wide receivers behind Drake London (55). Dotson has two catches or fewer in six of the first seven games of the regular season and has a 12-242-2 receiving line on 26 targets this year. The Falcons hit the road in Week 8 for an NFC South tilt…

items.h: Jahan Dotson catches one short pass in Sunday's win
items.s: Jahan Dotson caught 1-of-3 targets for only six yards in Sunday's 29-20 win over the 49ers. Dotson has become a big-play wideout for the Falcons, as he had averaged nearly 28 yards on his seven total grabs over the previous three weeks headed into Sunday's game. He had also found the end zone twice in that stretch. However, as should be expected going forward, Dotson showed in this contest that he is a boom-or-bust fantasy option in the Falcons' passing attack.

items.h: Jahan Dotson Trending Up, but Still a Boom/Bust Flex Option in Week 7
items.s: Atlanta Falcons wide receiver Jahan Dotson garnered five targets in Week 6, converting them into three catches for 87 yards and a score, his second touchdown of the season, with both of them coming in the last three games. The Penn State product has had at least 54 yards receiving in each of the last three games and has become the team's deep threat. The former first-rounder owns a 16.6 average depth of target (ADOT), which is more than six yards longer than Drake London's ADOT (10.0), and has earned 34.3 percent of the team's air yards through six weeks. Week 7's matchup could prove challenging, though, as the San Francisco defense is allowing just 209.8 yards passing per game…

items.h: Jahan Dotson Establishing Himself as Clear WR2 in Atlanta
items.s: Atlanta Falcons wide receiver Jahan Dotson is clearly establishing himself as the team's No. 2 pass-catcher behind Drake London. The 26-year-old caught three of a season-high five targets for a team-high 87 yards and his second touchdown of the season in Sunday's 31-23 loss at home to the Chicago Bears in Week 6. It was Dotson's second time finding the end zone in the last three weeks, and he has now gone over 50 receiving yards in each of the last three weeks after catching only four passes on 11 targets for 41 yards without a touchdown in the first three contests of the 2026 campaign. The Falcons do not have a very appealing Week 7 matchup against the 6-0 San Francisco 49ers, but Dotson…

items.h: Reaches end zone in defeat
items.s: Dotson caught three of five targets for 87 yards and a touchdown during Sunday's 31-23 loss to Chicago. Dotson led the team in receiving yards, and his most notable moment of the game came in the second quarter when he connected with quarterback Michael Penix for a 13-yard touchdown. The wide receiver has now reeled in multiple passes in three straight contests, exceeding 50 receiving yards in each of those games, and he appears to have distanced himself as the team's No. 2 option behind Drake London at his position.

items.h: Jahan Dotson finds end zone in Week 6 loss
items.s: Jahan Dotson hauled in three of his five targets for 87 yards and one touchdown in the Falcons' 31-23 Week 6 loss to the Chicago Bears. Dotson has made the most of his opportunities in the Atlanta passing offense of late, finishing with over 50 receiving yards in each of his last three contests. The wideout will look to offer head coach another stable pass-catching option moving forward, with a Week 7 contest against the San Francisco 49ers up next.

items.h: Jahan Dotson a Low-Floor, Low-Ceiling Play in Week 6
items.s: Atlanta Falcons wide receiver Jahan Dotson has become more interesting for fantasy managers over the last two weeks, recording exactly 54 receiving yards in each game while catching one touchdown pass. The downside is that he's caught no more than two passes in any game this season and received no more than four targets. Still, the 26-year-old has become the team's deep threat, with an average depth of target (ADOT) of 16.4 yards, compared to Drake London, whose 9.1-yard ADOT is second-best on the team. Even so, Dotson's limited involvement and dependency on big plays make the Penn State product a risky fantasy play most weeks. The Bears defense will be without multiple key defenders this…

items.h: Reels in 36-yard catch in OT loss
items.s: Dotson caught two of four passes for 54 yards during the Falcons' 30-23 overtime loss to the Ravens on Sunday. Dotson was responsible for the Falcons' second-longest play of the game, when he connected with Michael Penix (ribs) on a 36-yard pass late in the second quarter that led to a five-yard touchdown pass from Penix to Kyle Pitts three players later. Dotson finished as the Falcons' second-leading receiver behind Drake London (118), though Dotson's four targets were fourth-most on Atlanta behind London (11), Bijan Robinson (seven) and Pitts (six). Dotson is up to an 8-149-1 receiving line on 18 targets through five regular-season games, although the scoring ceilings for the Falcons…

items.h: Jahan Dotson finishes with 54 receiving yards in Week 5
items.s: Jahan Dotson caught 2-of-4 targets for 54 yards in Sunday's 30-23 OT loss to the Ravens. Dotson made a couple of big grabs in Sunday's game, but he remained no higher than the fourth option in the Falcons' passing attack. Dotson is averaging 18.6 yards per reception and caught his only touchdown so far this season in Week 4. That TD came off the arm of Michael Penix, who is now dealing with a rib injury.

items.h: Jahan Dotson Remains a Speculative Play Despite Scoring Last Week
items.s: Atlanta Falcons wide receiver Jahan Dotson found the end zone for the first time this season in last week's victory over the Saints, giving him one more than fellow WR Drake London and making him the only wide receiver on the team with a touchdown reception through the team's first four games. The Penn State product's 14 targets thus far are the third-most on the team, sitting comfortably ahead of Kyle Pitts Sr., who has the fourth-most with just nine targets. Still, the 5-foot-11 wideout can't be trusted on a weekly basis yet, and would be a risky fantasy play in Week 5 despite the Ravens missing LB Trey Hendrickson (finger) this week and potentially CB Marlon Humphrey (calf/hamstring) as…

items.h: Dotson caught two of three passes for 54 yards and a touchdown during the Falcons' 45-24 win over the Saints on Monday.
items.s: Falcons running backs Bijan Robinson and Brian Robinson were responsible for five of the team's six offensive touchdowns during Monday's blowout win, with the duo combining for 207 yards on 33 carries. Dotson was the only pass catcher to get in on the scoring action, with the fifth-year wideout connecting with Michael Penix on a 31-yard touchdown pass early in the fourth quarter to extend Atlanta's lead to 38-17. It was Dotson's first touchdown since Week 8 of the 2025 season, and he's up to a 6-95-1 receiving line (on 14 targets) through the first four games of the 2026 regular season. Up…

items.h: Dotson caught one pass on three targets for 11 yards during the Falcons' 35-14 win over the Packers on Thursday.
items.s: Dotson's three targets from Michael Penix were actually second-most on the Falcons behind Drake London (10), with Dotson finishing tied for the third-most receiving yards on the team. He's played over 60 percent of offensive snaps in each of the first three games of the regular season but has a 4-41-0 receiving line (on 11 targets) to show for it. That said, Dotson's scoring floor could steadily increase as the season progresses and Penix gets more reps under his belt. The Falcons will stay on the road for a Week 4 NFC South tilt against the Saints on Monday, Oct. 5.

items.h: Dotson caught two of four targets for 11 yards in Sunday's 34-3 loss to the Panthers.
items.s: Dotson was on the field for 52 of the team's 69 offensive snaps, but it didn't really matter much as the Falcons put together another putrid offensive performance. The wide receiver will look to be more productive with Michael Penix (knee) making his return to action Thursday night against the Packers.

items.h: Dotson caught one of three targets for 19 yards in Atlanta's 20-13 loss to the Steelers on Sunday.
items.s: Dotson acted as the clear WR2 behind Drake London, out-snapping rookie Zachariah Branch 38 to 18. Olamide Zaccheaus also played 18 offensive snaps. Dotson ran 19 routes to Zaccheaus' nine and Branch's six. None of these three figure to have any consistent fantasy viability as long as all three of London, Kyle Pitts and Bijan Robinson are healthy.

items.h: Dotson caught all three of his targets for 27 yards in Friday's 17-12 preseason win over the Dolphins.
items.s: Dotson accounted for three of Tua Tagovailoa's seven completions while Atlanta's starters were in the game, with three going to TE Kyle Pitts and one going to RB Brian Robinson. Offensive stars Bijan Robinson and Drake London sat out the preseason finale, but Dotson's involvement Friday suggests the 2022 first-round pick of the Commanders is positioned as the Falcons' No. 2 wideout behind London heading into the regular season.

items.h: Dotson is playing with Atlanta's first-team offense at training camp, Will McFadden of the Falcons' official site reports.
items.s: Dotson has featured with the starters consistently, working alongside Drake London while Olamide Zaccheaus and Zachariah Branch rotate in. In the process, McFadden notes that Dotson had a nice gain on a crossing route early in the full-team period of Thursday's practice. The 16th overall pick in the 2022 NFL Draft has recorded 1,519 receiving yards and 12 touchdowns through four NFL regular seasons split between Washington and Philadelphia, with seven of those scores coming in Dotson's rookie campaign.

items.h: Dotson is set to compete for slotting in a "wide open" Atlanta wideout depth chart behind Drake London, Bobby Kownack of NFL.com reports.
items.s: Dotson had some solid stretches early in his career with Washington, but his production dropped dramatically after he was traded to the Eagles ahead of the 2024 season. Of course, Philadelphia had the stud wideout duo of A.J. Brown and DeVonta Smith hogging most of Jalen Hurts' targets and consequently impeding Dotson's opportunities. Things are a bit different for the Penn State product after he signed with Atlanta in early March -- though London (undisclosed) is the team's clear alpha at wideout, the No. 2 slot in the WR pecking order is probably going to come down to whoever wins the…

items.h: Dotson and the Falcons have reached agreement on a two-year contract, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.
items.s: Schefter reports it as a two-year, $15 million deal, including $10 million guaranteed at signing. The contract suggests Dotson will compete for a starting job, after he spent two seasons in Philadelphia as a lightly targeted No. 3 WR (37 catches in 34 regular-season games) behind A.J. Brown and DeVonta Smith. A 2022 first-round pick, Dotson will turn 26 in March and now figures to compete with fellow free-agent signing Olamide Zaccheaus for playing time alongside No. 1 receiver Drake London.

items.h: Dotson finished his second season with the Eagles with a total of 18 receptions for 262 yards and one touchdown in 17 regular-season games.
items.s: Dotson's numbers were very similar to last year's 19 catches for 216 yards and zero scores, a big step down from his average of 42 catches for 520.5 yards and 5.5 touchdowns in his first two years in the league with Washington. If he remains stuck behind A.J. Brown and DeVonta Smith in Philadelphia again next season, expect similar production.

items.h: Dotson finished with zero catches on one target in Sunday's 13-12 win over the Bills.
items.s: Dotson has now been held without a catch on six different occasions this season and has caught exactly one pass seven times. If the Eagles rest their starters in next week's regular-season finale against the Commanders, he could play a larger role, but with the second seed still a possibility with a win and a Bears loss, that may not be the plan.

items.h: Dotson caught three passes on as many targets for 13 yards during the Eagles' 29-18 win over the Commanders on Saturday.
items.s: A.J. Brown (12 targets) and DeVonta Smith (eight targets) dominated the looks from Jalen Hurts during Saturday's win. Dotson got into the action with two catches during the Eagles' first offensive drive of the second half, and he would have had a five-yard touchdown catch to his name had it not been nullified by an offensive holding penalty. Dotson has not seen more than three targets in a game this season, and he'll carry a 15-222-1 line (on 27 targets) into the Eagles' Week 16 road tilt against the Bills on Sunday, Dec. 28. With Philadelphia locked in as the NFC East champions, it's…

items.h: Dotson was not targeted a single time in Sunday's 31-0 win over the Raiders.
items.s: The lopsided stat line led to the Eagles rushing 47 times while attempting just 18 passes, so there weren't many targets to go around. Dotson typically doesn't see much action even when the Eagles need to pass, however, averaging just 1.7 targets and 0.9 catches per game this season.

items.h: Dotson caught one of three targets for three yards in Monday's 22-19 overtime loss to the Chargers.
items.s: Dotson caught just one of three targets for the second straight week, as the fourth-year wideout continues to see minimal usage in the Eagles struggling aerial attack. The 25-year-old should continue to operate as Philadelphia's No. 3 wide receiver, but this role is unlikely to produce much fantasy value down the stretch. Next up for the Eagles is a Week 15 matchup against the Raiders.

items.h: Dotson (toe) doesn't have a designation for Monday's game at the Chargers.
items.s: Dotson was limited in the first two practices of Week 14 prep due to a toe injury, but his return to all activity Saturday has him in the clear for Monday. In 12 games this season, he's had a few splash plays but mustered just a cumulative 11-206-1 line on 21 targets while working behind the top WR duo of A.J. Brown and DeVonta Smith.

items.h: Dotson (toe) remained limited at Friday's practice, Andrew DiCecco of InsideTheBirds.com reports.
items.s: Dotson has one more chance to upgrade to full participation ahead of Monday's matchup with the Chargers. He was listed as a limited participant both Thursday and Friday.

items.h: Dotson (toe) was a limited participant in practice Thursday.
items.s: It appears to be a new issue for the wide receiver, who played 31 offensive snaps on Black Friday against Chicago. Dotson's status will be worth monitoring as the practice week continues ahead of Monday night's matchup with the Chargers. The fourth-year pro has 11 catches for 206 yards and a touchdown this year.

items.h: Dotson caught one of three targets for 12 yards in Friday's 24-15 loss to the Bears.
items.s: Dotson tied his season high in targets and recorded the fourth-most receiving yards on the Eagles during Sunday's loss. The 25-year-old has played a minimal role on Philadelphia's offense this season, recording 206 receiving yards and one touchdown on 11 receptions across 12 games. He's likely to operate as the team's No. 3 wide receiver but carry minimal fantasy value in the Week 14 matchup against the Chargers.

items.h: Dotson failed to catch his lone target in Sunday's 24-21 loss to the Cowboys.
items.s: The 2022 first-round pick was targeted just once and went without a catch for the third time in the Eagles' last five games during Sunday's loss. Dotson has appeared in all 11 of Philadelphia's games this season, catching 10 of 18 targets for 194 yards and a touchdown across 359 offensive snaps. He's expected to operate as the Eagles' No. 3 wideout but carry minimal fantasy value in the Week 13 matchup against the Bears.

items.h: Dotson caught a pair of passes for 43 yards in Sunday's 16-9 victory over the Lions.
items.s: Dotson's second catch of the day, a 34-yard reception down the sideline after Jalen Hurts was forced out of the pocket, helped dig the Eagles out of tough field position on their own four-yard line late in the fourth quarter. He's made the occasional key play for the Eagles this season and is averaging an impressive 19.4 yards per catch, but he's caught a total of just 10 passes in 10 games. Sunday's contest marked just the second time all year that he's caught multiple passes.

items.h: Dotson failed to pull in his lone target in Monday's 10-7 victory over the Packers.
items.s: Dotson finished with zero catches for the second time in three games and the third time all year. He also saw the field for just 19 offensive snaps, his lowest total in two seasons as an Eagle. He has fewer receptions (eight) than games played (nine) this season.

items.h: Dotson made one catch on two targets for a 40-yard touchdown in Sunday's 38-20 win over the Giants.
items.s: Even with A.J. Brown (hamstring) ruled out, Dotson didn't see a significant increase in his role, but he made his opportunities count by hauling in Jalen Hurts' fourth TD of the day in the fourth quarter. The Eagles will get a Week 9 bye, which may give Brown enough time to get back onto the field, but if he remains sidelined in Week 10 against the Packers, Dotson could have some deep-league appeal.

items.h: Dotson wasn't targeted a single time in Sunday's 28-22 win over the Vikings.
items.s: Jalen Hurts threw for a season-high 326 yards, but Dotson wasn't able to benefit. DeVonta Smith and A.J. Brown combined for 304 of those yards, leaving even less than usual for the rest of Hurts' potential targets. Dotson has averaged one catch per game through seven games this season.

items.h: Dotson caught one of his two targets for 17 yards in Thursday's loss to the Giants.
items.s: One catch has become Dotson's typical stat line for the Eagles. He's finished with exactly one reception in four of six games this season and finished with exactly one catch in eight regular-season games last year.

items.h: Dotson caught one pass for 24 yards in Sunday's loss to the Broncos.
items.s: Dotson was on the field for 71 percent of the Eagles' offensive snaps, his second-highest snap share of the year, but it didn't result in a significant role. He's now been held to one or fewer catches in 19 of his 23 regular-season games with the Eagles over the last two years.

items.h: Dotson was not targeted a single time in Sunday's 31-25 win over the Buccaneers.
items.s: Dotson has rarely recorded more than one catch in a game during his two seasons with the Eagles, and he didn't even reach that low threshold Sunday. He's now been blanked seven times in 21 regular season games with the team.

items.h: Dotson caught one of his three targets for seven yards in Sunday's 33-26 win over the Rams.
items.s: After finishing Week 1 with three catches for 59 yards, Dotson has just one reception in both of the last two weeks. He did play a season-high 49 offensive snaps against the Rams, likely due to the fact that the Eagles were trailing for most of the game, but that didn't result in a large number of targets.

items.h: Dotson was held to one catch for four yards in Sunday's win over the Chiefs.
items.s: Dotson was the Eagles' leading receiver in Week 1, catching three passes for 59 yards, but his Week 2 performance is probably more in line with what can be expected going forward. Outside of a Week 18 game in which the Eagles rested their starters, Dotson averaged less than a catch per game last year, and with A.J. Brown and DeVonta Smith still ahead of him on the depth chart, that's unlikely to change.

items.h: Dotson caught all three of his targets for 59 yards in Thursday's 24-20 win over the Cowboys.
items.s: Most of Dotson's production came on a 51-yard catch in the second quarter, which was enough to make him the team's leading receiver in the Eagles' run-heavy Week 1 win. DeVonta Smith and A.J. Brown combined for just 24 yards on four targets. Those two likely will be more involved moving forward at Dotson's expense, but at least Dotson seems to have a firm grasp on the third spot on the wide receiver depth chart over trade acquisition John Metchie, who wasn't targeted Thursday.

items.h: Dotson caught both of his targets for 27 yards in Thursday's preseason game against Cincinnati.
items.s: Jimmy Kempski of PhillyVoice.com notes that Dotson and RG Tyler Steen were the only projected starters on offense to play for Philadelphia. It's not where Dotson imagined he'd be when Washington took him 16th overall in the 2022 NFL Draft, but he at least did his part to help Philly's second-string offense score a TD against Cincinnati's first-string defenders. The No. 3 WR role in Philadelphia isn't one where snaps are likely to translate to many targets, unless maybe the Eagles are missing a couple of their skill-position standouts (A.J. Brown, DeVonta Smith, Saquon Barkley, Dallas…

items.h: Dotson secured 19 of 33 targets for 216 yards across 17 regular-season games with the Eagles in 2024. He also rushed once for 13 yards.
items.s: Dotson played a sizeable 649 offensive snaps during the regular season for Philadelphia, working in a No. 3 receiver role behind A.J. Brown and DeVonta Smith. His most impactful game of the season came during the Eagles' win over Kansas City in Super Bowl LIX, with two catches for 42 yards on three targets. The 2022 first-round pick looks set to reprise a similar role for the 2025 season, though with all of Brown, Smith, running back Saquon Barkley and tight end Dallas Goedert pushing for opportunities on offense, he seems likely to again end up on the outside looking in for fantasy purposes.

items.h: Dotson reached the end zone for the first time as an Eagle in Sunday's wild-card win over the Packers, finishing with one catch for an 11-yard score.
items.s: The Eagles got off to a quick start in their 22-10 win, forcing a fumble on the opening kickoff and scoring just three plays later on second-and-9 from the 11. Jalen Hurts had nearly seven seconds in the pocket and found Dotson wide open at the back of the end zone for the wideout's first score since Week 11 of the 2023 season. The rest of the game was more typical for Dotson's time in Philadelphia, as he received just one more target and did not record a reception.

items.h: Dotson caught seven of 11 targets for 94 yards in Sunday's 20-13 win over the Giants.
items.s: Working as the Eagles' No. 1 receiver while A.J. Brown and DeVonta Smith were rested ahead of the playoffs, Dotson had by far his best game of the year and his most productive day since he erupted for an 8-108-1 line in Week 8 last season against Philly as a member of the Commanders. Dotson hadn't even caught a pass since Week 14 prior to his Week 18 breakout, however, and he'll likely return to being an afterthought in the Eagles' passing game next weekend in the wild-card round against the Packers.

items.h: Dotson was not targeted a single time in Sunday's 41-7 blowout win over the Cowboys.
items.s: Dotson has now gone without a catch in three straight contests and has earned a total of just one target over that stretch. His role could expand in Week 18 if the Eagles rest their starters with nothing left to play for, but he'll need five catches to even average one reception per game for the season. He has 12 receptions in 16 contests thus far.

items.h: Dotson finished with zero catches for the second straight week Sunday against the Commanders.
items.s: Dotson's two chances at a revenge game this season have led to a combined one catch for eight yards. To be fair to Dotson, the Eagles leaned heavily on the run Sunday after Jalen Hurts exited early with a concussion, completing a total of just 15 passes. All but one of those went to A.J. Brown or DeVonta Smith.

items.h: Dotson finished with zero receptions on one target in Sunday's 27-13 win over the Steelers.
items.s: The game ended a streak of six straight contests in which Dotson recorded exactly one catch. The Eagles' passing game was the primary story surrounding the team during the week, and Jalen Hurts responded with a strong performance, going 25-of-32 for 290 yards and two touchdowns, but as usual, nearly all of his looks went to his top two wideouts. A.J. Brown and DeVonta Smith each saw double-digit targets, while the rest of the team combined for just eight.

items.h: Dotson caught one of his two targets for five yards in Sunday's 22-16 win over the Panthers.
items.s: Week 14 marked the sixth straight game in which Dotson has caught just one pass. The third-year wideout played 24 of the Eagles 58 offensive snaps, the lowest snap share of any Philadelphia wide receiver in the contest behind A.J. Brown (55), DeVonta Smith (52) and Johnny Wilson (29). With such limited playing time in a run-heavy offensive scheme, Dotson remains off the fantasy radar heading into a Week 15 matchup against the Steelers.

items.h: Dotson caught one pass for seven yards in Sunday's 24-19 win over the Ravens.
items.s: Even with DeVonta Smith (hamstring) out of action, Dotson failed to make much of an impact, finishing with precisely one catch for the fifth straight game. The Eagles found more success on the ground than through the air, completing just 11 passes on the day.

items.h: Fantasy football Shadow Report: Key WR/CB matchups for NFL Week 13
items.s: Find out which wide receivers to upgrade, downgrade and avoid this week with a special WR vs. CB cheat sheet.

items.h: Dotson caught one pass for four yards in Sunday's 37-20 win over the Rams.
items.s: Dotson has now caught exactly one pass in four straight games. His yardage on his lone reception has decreased each week, going from 36 to 27 to eight to four. Expect a single reception for roughly one yard next week if the pattern continues.

items.h: Fantasy football Shadow Report: Key WR/CB matchups for NFL Week 12
items.s: Find out which wide receivers to upgrade, downgrade and avoid this week with a special WR vs. CB cheat sheet.

items.h: Dotson finished with one catch for eight yards in Thursday's win over the Commanders.
items.s: Dotson has now finished with exactly one catch in three straight games. That's technically better than average for him this season, as he's caught nine passes through 10 games, an average of 0.9 per contest.

items.h: Dotson finished with one catch for 27 yards in Sunday's 34-6 win at Dallas.
items.s: Jalen Hurts found Dotson deep down the right sideline early in the second quarter but did not look his way the rest of the game. It's the second straight week in which Dotson has finished with a single long reception. He's totaled 98 yards on eight catches in nine games played this season.

items.h: Dotson made a spectacular catch for a 36-yard gain on his only target early in the third quarter of Sunday's win over the Jaguars.
items.s: A.J. Brown left with a knee injury shortly before halftime, and Dotson received his one opportunity of the game shortly after the break, reaching over Tyson Campbell's back on a long pass down the left and tipping the ball up to himself to make the grab. Jalen Hurts didn't look Dotson's way again the rest of the game, however, and the receiver's workload may be limited again in Week 10 against the Cowboys if Brown's injury proves minor. Brown's tests came back clean after the game and he appears to have a real chance to return without missing any time, but that's not yet guaranteed.

items.h: Dotson was not targeted in Sunday's 37-17 win over Cincinnati.
items.s: The Eagles prioritized the run on Sunday, especially after opening up a second-half lead, with Jalen Hurts attempting just 20 passes. As usual, A.J. Brown and DeVonta Smith soaked up most of the targets, with other Eagles combining for just six, none of which went to Dotson. The third-year wideout has just six catches in seven games this season.
